decisions.title: Installed host release and catch-up baseline
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback and baseline edit. Bottom line: record the installed 0.84.3 host release with no ce-workflow source change. Verified project fit: ce-workflow uses Pi extension hooks and sendUserMessage but does not import the renamed Google thinking type. Verified upstream evidence: the installed changelog and captured 0.84.2-to-0.84.3 artifact document the release. Benefit: inherit safer extension rollback, compaction/tool/runtime fixes, session-scoped model and thinking controls, and Windows support. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt the release baseline.

decisions.title: Add native PowerShell to ce-workflow defaults
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1. Bottom line: keep existing Bash and explicit PowerShell command paths; do not widen every workflow tool set. Verified project fit: ce-workflow already runs its Windows commands through supported shell paths and has no coded native PowerShell-tool dependency. Upstream evidence: 0.84.3 makes PowerShell optional rather than replacing Bash. Benefit: avoids an unused tool and schema. Cost/risk: none until a concrete PowerShell-only operation appears. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local change.

decisions.title: Duplicate goal recovery on session_compact_failed
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not add a second compaction recovery owner for this patch. Verified project fit: ce-workflow already has tested retry, overflow, agent-end, and settled-boundary recovery with stale-continuation guards. Upstream evidence: 0.84.3 exposes session_compact_failed as additive telemetry. Benefit: avoids duplicate continuation scheduling. Cost/risk: the new event is not consumed locally. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the existing single recovery path unless a concrete missed-failure reproduction appears.

decisions.title: Host-owned provider, model, update, and runtime changes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit model catalogs, thinking controls, managed updates, startup optimizations, provider fixes, and TUI behavior without adapters. Verified project fit: these surfaces are owned by Pi and ce-workflow has no conflicting type import or installer implementation. Benefit: keeps ce-workflow smaller. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code.

decisions.title: Verified private workflow generation
decisions.rationale: The official stable release is translated into the complete private nine-workflow generation with no ordinary CE runtime surface.

decisions.title: Workflow reliability, recovery, and smaller child context release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 baseline-only record and package rollback. Bottom line: record installed 0.58.0 with no ce-workflow source change. Verified project fit: ce-workflow agents use replacement prompts plus explicit project-context settings, so the new default of not inheriting the operator's global context does not remove their contracts; existing inline workflowScript and RPC paths remain supported. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.53.0-to-0.58.0 changelog, public extension API, and captured artifact document the release. Benefit: inherit safer recovery, model and fast-mode handling, workflow validation, MCP support, diagnostics, and smaller child context. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and advance only this package's baseline.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-subagents changelog reports 0.58.0; agent frontmatter inspection confirms explicit replacement prompts and project-context policy; captured 0.52.0-to-0.58.0 artifact reviewed

decisions.title: Replace packaged agent discovery with runtime registration
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: retain the small packaged-agent directory exposure. Verified project fit: ce-workflow ships many file-backed agents with frontmatter, skills, and prompts; the current helper adds one directory once. Verified upstream evidence: runtime registration accepts programmatic definitions and is process-local. Benefit: no meaningful deletion because ce-workflow would need to parse and register every definition plus cleanup. Cost/risk: replacing the current path would add lifecycle code and duplicate package parsing. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local change.

decisions.title: Move current workflows to workflowScriptPath
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1. Bottom line: keep generated inline workflow scripts for dynamic role orchestration. Verified project fit: repository call sites build bounded scripts from current runtime state and have no reusable static workflow file. Verified upstream evidence: workflowScriptPath is additive and intended for reusable script files. Benefit: avoids creating files that would merely mirror dynamic strings. Cost/risk: none until a stable repeated script exists. Confidence: high. Recommendation: do not add scaffolding.

decisions.title: Package-owned runner, MCP, model, recovery, and UI changes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit external runners, MCP resolution, fast mode, model exclusions, recovery handoffs, status, Fleet, and context-isolation behavior without adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow consumes the public subagent tool and RPC boundaries rather than package internals. Benefit: keeps one lifecycle owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local source change.

decisions.title: Responsive decision UI and Herdr attention signaling
decisions.rationale: Responsive list layouts and blocked/waiting attention signals are implemented inside pi-ask-user and inherited by ce-workflow's existing ask_user calls. Local dialog policy remains separate and no compatibility shim is required.

decisions.title: ask_user telemetry integration
decisions.rationale: The release exposes no stable per-call telemetry API, while ce-workflow already records tool timing and dialog decisions. Local wrapping would duplicate package behavior without measurable savings; revisit if a public metrics hook appears.

decisions.title: Scoped routing and consent-aware extension release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 baseline-only record and package rollback. Bottom line: record installed 0.12.0 with no ce-workflow source change. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's supervisor policy already uses exact sessions and explicit replies; the new scope boundary is opt-in, while enabling it by default would break intentional cross-project supervision. Verified upstream evidence: the captured 0.11.0-to-0.12.0 artifact and installed public README document scoped routing, lazy visibility, and the consent-aware extension outbox. Benefit: inherit scoped routing, consent-aware outbox support, broker hardening, and optional lazy visibility. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and retain current unscoped and always-visible behavior.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-intercom package manifest is 0.12.0; captured 0.11.0-to-0.12.0 public API and README artifact reviewed

decisions.title: Enable a broker scope by default
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1 environment change. Bottom line: keep sessions unscoped by default. Verified project fit: ce-workflow intentionally coordinates supervising and target sessions across project directories and relies on exact IDs for trust. Verified upstream evidence: PI_INTERCOM_SCOPE_ID is an opt-in hard routing boundary. Benefit: preserves current cross-project supervision while users can opt into isolation. Cost/risk: unscoped sessions retain existing visibility. Confidence: high. Recommendation: do not set a project-wide scope.

decisions.title: Hide intercom until first use
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1 config change. Bottom line: retain always-visible intercom for ce-workflow sessions. Verified project fit: supervisor coordination may be the first action after a delayed message or trust-sensitive handoff. Verified upstream evidence: after-first-use visibility intentionally hides the generic tool until an inbound message, overlay send, or skill load. Benefit: avoids making required coordination availability stateful. Cost/risk: keeps one tool schema active. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local config change.

decisions.title: Replace agent-authored coordination with extension outbox sends
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: keep trust-sensitive coordination explicit and agent-authored. Verified project fit: ce-workflow requires the agent to inspect pending asks and durable state before replying; a coded outbox cannot make that judgment. Verified upstream evidence: the outbox is consent-aware and terminally acknowledged but does not replace message policy. Benefit: avoids a second message owner. Cost/risk: coded notifications do not use the new seam. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local integration.

decisions.title: Broker scope, outbox, routing, and UI internals
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit broker hardening, scoped mailbox behavior, provenance, and UI/config support without adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow owns coordination policy, not intercom transport or storage. Benefit: safer package-owned delivery. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code.

decisions.title: Independent goal safety and coexistence release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 baseline-only record and package rollback. Bottom line: record installed 0.54.3 as an independently owned goal extension; do not replace or integrate ce-workflow's domain-specific autonomous engine. Verified project fit: this repository has no pi-goal dependency or command/event callsite, while ce-workflow's goal loop owns work-item, verifier, catch-up, compaction, and completion gates. Verified upstream evidence: the captured 0.52.1-to-0.54.3 artifact and installed README document stable goal tools, safety limits, a built runtime, and cooperative workflow mutex behavior. Benefit: acknowledge the installed package's stable tools, safety limits, mutex behavior, and built runtime. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now as no-local-action.
decisions.verification: Installed @narumitw/pi-goal package manifest is 0.54.3; captured 0.52.1-to-0.54.3 README and public runtime artifact reviewed; repository search found no integration callsite

decisions.title: Replace ce-workflow autonomous goals with pi-goal
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 3 after state and command migration. Bottom line: pi-goal remains a generic single-objective loop, not a substitute for ce-workflow's work-item, verifier, catch-up, lease, and completion gates. Verified project fit: ce-workflow enforces domain state before completion and has distinct human-decision and safety paths. Verified upstream evidence: 0.54.3 exposes generic goal_complete, goal_blocked, goal_wait, and optional managed-run behavior. Benefit: avoids deleting required domain guarantees for superficial code reduction. Cost/risk: the purpose-built engine remains. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no replacement.

decisions.title: Add workflow mutex integration without a reproduced collision
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not add an optional coordination protocol without evidence that ce-workflow and pi-goal contend in supported use. Verified project fit: ce-workflow does not invoke pi-goal and the package is not a dependency. Verified upstream evidence: the mutex is cooperative and its documented coexistence guarantee is characterized for pi-goal with plan mode, not ce-workflow. Benefit: avoids speculative lifecycle state. Cost/risk: independently activated workflow extensions can still conflict if a user deliberately runs both. Confidence: high. Recommendation: revisit only with a concrete collision reproduction.

decisions.title: Goal package UI, persistence, safety, and build internals
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit package-owned tool visibility, state restoration, limits, mutex participation, and bundled runtime behavior without adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow has no pi-goal API consumer. Benefit: keeps ownership clear. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code.

decisions.title: Diagnostics, read-guard, graph, and observability release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 baseline-only record and package rollback. Bottom line: record installed 4.1.2 and inherit its diagnostics, read-guard, opaque-write, LSP, graph, parser, and telemetry fixes without changing ce-workflow's optional integration boundary. Verified project fit: ce-workflow only availability-gates project_report for its isolated verifier and does not programmatically invoke pi-lens schemas; immutable checkpoint verification remains on work_verifier tools rather than live symbol tools. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 4.1.2 changelog and captured 4.0.1-to-4.1.2 artifact document the release. Benefit: safer and more observable code intelligence automatically. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now with no local source change.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-lens changelog reports 4.1.2; captured 4.0.1-to-4.1.2 artifact reviewed; repository integration remains availability-gated

decisions.title: Add optional pi-lens tools to every durable role allowlist
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not make durable roles depend on an optional ambient extension. Verified project fit: explicit role allowlists must remain launchable without pi-lens, while the lens verifier is selected only after a coded availability check. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.2 improves package tools and runners but does not change ce-workflow's optional dependency boundary. Benefit: preserves role availability. Cost/risk: roles continue using native targeted reads unless pi-lens is present. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the current boundary.

decisions.title: Use live symbol tools inside immutable checkpoint verification
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: keep immutable findings on checkpoint-scoped verifier tools. Verified project fit: module_report and read_symbol inspect the live workspace, while verifier findings must bind to a recorded snapshot. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.2 strengthens live read guards and graph freshness but does not make these tools checkpoint readers. Benefit: avoids time-of-check/time-of-use drift. Cost/risk: checkpoint reads remain deliberately bounded. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no verifier expansion.

decisions.title: Package-owned scanners, parsers, LSP, graph, cache, and runtime fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit opaque-write recovery, parser hardening, late auxiliary findings, freshness, graph, LSP, cache, telemetry, and lifecycle fixes without adapters. Verified project fit: these are implemented behind pi-lens's public tool results and diagnostics pipeline. Benefit: avoids duplicating package internals. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code.
